details: Ethereum's significant Glamsterdam upgrade, designed to enhance scalability and efficiency through features like enshrined proposer-builder separation and block-level access lists, has gone live on the Sepolia testnet. This marks one of the final testnet activations before its mainnet launch, though the gas limit on Sepolia was initially lower than the 200 million target, indicating further development.
title: Ethereum's Glamsterdam Upgrade Launches on Sepolia Testnet

details: Ethereum successfully executed its first atomic Layer 1 (L1) to Layer 2 (L2) transaction on the mainnet, a major milestone for cross-layer execution. This achievement is expected to significantly improve the network's scalability and overall usability for decentralized applications and users.
title: Ethereum Achieves First Atomic L1-to-L2 Transaction

details: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has proposed its first formal crypto-market rules, Regulations CTX and CAM, aiming to establish a federal regulatory scheme for crypto exchanges. This move comes after the failure of the Clarity Act in Congress and seeks to provide a unified federal approach rather than a fragmented state-by-state licensing system.
title: CFTC Proposes Federal Framework for Crypto Regulation

details: Bitcoin (BTC) has been trading around the mid-$80,000s, showing strength at the start of October, a month historically known as "Uptober" for positive BTC performance. The cryptocurrency is nearing the $88,000 mark, where a cluster of leveraged short positions could trigger a short squeeze, potentially pushing BTC towards $90,000-$93,000. Easing expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, due to softer U.S. labor data, are providing support for risk assets like Bitcoin. The 2026 yearly open at $87,570 remains a key resistance level.
title: Bitcoin Nears $88,000 Amid Bullish October Sentiment and Short Squeeze Potential

details: The U.S. Treasury Department has withdrawn two previously proposed rules: the 2023 crypto-mixing rule and the 2020 self-hosted wallet rule. These proposals would have required identity checks and reporting for transfers to unhosted wallets. The withdrawal is seen as a relief for privacy advocates and those concerned about stringent regulations on self-custody.
title: US Treasury Withdraws Crypto Mixer and Self-Hosted Wallet Rules

details: Genius Group (GNS) has resumed its Bitcoin treasury acquisitions, purchasing 10 BTC between October 2 and October 5, 2026, for approximately $854,000. This is part of the company's approved $1.2 billion dual treasury capital plan, which allocates funds to both Bitcoin and AI assets.
title: Genius Group Recommences Bitcoin Treasury Purchases

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed new rules to establish a tailored framework for the custody of crypto assets by registered investment advisers and regulated funds. The proposal aims to modernize existing custody rules, increase investor choice, and allow self-custody under specific conditions, as well as permit the use of state trust companies as custodians. (Note: This news item was published on October 1, 2026, but is highly relevant to ongoing market discussions and regulatory clarity.)
title: SEC Proposes New Crypto Custody Rules for Investment Advisers
